gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Dometic CFX3 25 fridge ChatGPT showed on a card is $699.99 and listed as out of stock on Dometic's US page today, or that the BLUETTI AC180 is $499 at BLUETTI today, not $449. That makes the setup ChatGPT showed about $1,199, while the $369 EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro (768 Wh) already runs that same fridge for about 59 h.
standout_why: I compared willitrunpower.com, which names models and works out runtimes but gives no prices (only 'Check price on Amazon' links), and our own Nov 3 page, which ChatGPT quoted at $449 for the AC180 and which has no fridge prices or stock status. ChatGPT's searches in chat pl-044 found only EcoFlow and ICECO manuals and EcoFlow product pages. None of these pages totals station plus fridge or flags that the Dometic is out of stock. The GOES and Stanislaus County HSA pages are about medical guidance and name no products.
decides: The pick changes. The Dometic CFX3 25 draws 0.92 Ah/h at 90°F, so a 768 Wh station is enough for 48 h. That makes the 1,152 Wh AC180 more battery than needed. The value setup is the RIVER 2 Pro at $369 plus a 12 V compressor fridge, as long as the fridge can actually be bought. The Dometic is $699.99 and out of stock at Dometic US. The cheaper BougeRV 23 qt ($169.99) can't be confirmed for 48 h because its maker gives no average daily draw. The Elite 100 V2 costs the same $499 as the AC180 but holds 128 Wh less, so the AC180 wins between the two. The Elite 30 V2 (288 Wh) and the BougeRV CRX3 with its built-in battery (up to 29 h) both fall short of 48 h.
